title: Development and Validation of the CervantesPROM, a New Menopause-Specific Quality-of-Life Measure
official: Official Title Development and Psychometric Validation of the CervantesPROM, a New Patient-Reported Outcome Measure (PROM) of Health-Related Quality of Life in Women During the Peri and Postmenopause
summary:
The Cervantes Scale and its short form (Cervantes-SF) have been the reference instruments for measuring menopause-related quality of life in Spain for two decades, but they do not capture several of today's most prevalent symptoms (weight and body changes, mood lability, cognitive complaints, dyspareunia), they confound the presence or intensity of a symptom with its actual impact, and they contain socioculturally outdated items.

This study develops and psychometrically validates the CervantesPROM, a new self-administered, digital patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) of health-related quality of life for women aged 35 to 75 years in the menopausal transition and postmenopause, following Classical Test Theory and COSMIN standards. For each symptom, the instrument records separately whether it is present and how much it bothers the woman in daily life, which is the dimension scored for quality of life.

The project has three phases: item generation and content validity (Phase 1, completed with an expert panel), item reduction and psychometric validation (Phases 2A and 2B), and responsiveness (Phase 3). Reference values for the Spanish population are an objective of the linked SILVA study, which has its own registration.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Women aged 35 to 75 years, living in Spain.
* Late reproductive stage (regular cycles with a change in menstrual flow), perimenopause or postmenopause, including early menopause and premature ovarian insufficiency; or a stage not classifiable by menstrual criteria because of hysterectomy, endometrial ablation or hormonal contraception.
* Able to understand and complete a self-administered questionnaire in Spanish.
* Informed consent.
* Phase 3 only: physician's indication to start treatment for menopausal symptoms (the study does not intervene in that decision).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Regular menstrual cycles with no menstrual change and no climacteric symptoms.
* Active cancer under oncological treatment (a history of treated cancer is not an exclusion criterion).
* Active or decompensated severe disease, or hospital admission in the previous 3 months (stable chronic conditions such as hypertension, diabetes or hypothyroidism are not excluded).
* Active severe psychiatric disorder that prevents understanding or completing the questionnaire (treatment with antidepressants or anxiolytics alone is not an exclusion criterion).
* Phase 2A only: current menopausal hormone therapy or combined hormonal contraception (pill, ring or patch). Progestogen-only methods, including the levonorgestrel intrauterine system, are eligible.
